category_title: Older preschool children expressing specific anxieties about environmental and relational consistency
minimal_context: The student is participating in a journal writing activity to reflect on the upcoming move to a new school.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's work on our feeling journals today. Please draw or write about the upcoming move to the new school.

STUDENT: (Looking at the pictures of the current preschool) I feel a little nervous. This is where we did this project.

TUTOR: Just write down what you are thinking about.

STUDENT: I will miss the playground because I would play here.

TUTOR: Keep drawing in your journal.

STUDENT: (Pushes the journal away) I don’t want to move. I like this school.

options.A: Complete a check-in with the student, finding ways for them to nonverbally or verbally express their feelings about the transition through the feeling journal or conversation.
options.B: Withhold attention when the student engages in the problem behavior of pushing the journal away, ensuring no verbal or physical response is provided to the student.
options.C: Follow through to ensure the student complies with the direction to keep drawing, physically helping them complete the journal entry if they do not do it independently.
options.D: Terminate the journal writing demands immediately and remove the feeling journal and drawing materials from the student's workspace for a brief period of ten seconds.
